description:
CHITRA is a team brought together by curiosity, creativity, and a shared passion for space. We believe great ideas come from different skills, experiences, and ways of thinking.

We’re here to learn, build, and turn ideas into reality. 🚀
summary: We built AREO Marswalk Studio, an offline Windows planner for crews exploring western Jezero Crater. Our team chose Jezero and shaped the workflow around a practical question: can we reach a science site and return with enough EVA reserve and daylight? Tap a measured point to preview a round trip, inspect its local XYZ coordinates, or mark a reported obstacle to recalculate the route. We combined a registered Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter CTX image and USGS stereo elevation model with Perseverance surface imagery and CRISM mineral context. Testing the app ourselves exposed a limitation in the original fixed-stop workflow, so we added tap-to-route for any measured point in the loaded area.
details:
TEAM CONTRIBUTION: Our project lead proposed the offline Marswalk planner, set the Windows and offline requirements, helped shape the architecture, and directed feature choices including local XYZ coordinates, a Mars sol clock, and return planning. We checked the app hands-on, asked how a crew would use it, and used that feedback to improve the workflow. The tap-to-route feature came from noticing that the original map made it too hard to choose an arbitrary destination.

SCIENCE GOAL: We chose western Jezero to compare sedimentary textures at a proposed transect with the larger shape of the ancient delta. MRO CTX provides orbital context, CRISM adds published mineral context, and Perseverance Mastcam-Z shows the surface at rover scale.

WORKFLOW: Select a habitat and tap a destination. AREO previews a round trip over measured DEM samples. The offline A* engine enforces a sampled grade limit and avoids missing-data and crew-reported exclusion cells. The return tool uses a reported crew position and elapsed time to estimate the quickest modeled walk back and check EVA reserve and daylight. NASA GISS Mars24 equations drive the local solar clocks. JSON export keeps the route and its assumptions together.

IMPLEMENTATION: React, TypeScript, Vite, and Electron. Windows build and demo: https://github.com/arnavgupta714/AREO-Marswalk-Studio/releases/tag/submission-v1.2.0

LIMITS: The offline pack covers about 5.64 × 4.76 km of western Jezero. The 40–60 m DEM sampling can miss rocks, drop-offs, or shadows. Habitat and science stops are proposed. Crew position is entered manually.

SI DISCLOSURE: We used OpenAI Codex to help explore ideas, research source data, implement and debug features, run technical checks, and prepare submission text and demo captions. We used an image generator for an early UI concept that is excluded from the submitted source snapshot. The shipped app uses credited NASA/USGS observations and Team CHITRA’s supplied logo. AREO calculates routes and local Mars time using deterministic algorithms.
